$comment: Bundled blocklist for the `local-blocklist` check. Hosts, lowercased, no scheme, no path.
SHIPPED CONTENT IS DELIBERATELY SYNTHETIC. Every entry below uses an RFC 2606 reserved name
(.invalid / .test / .example) so this file can never point at a live host — the same rule the
test fixtures follow. A real threat feed is a moving target and does not belong in git; it is
fetched into chrome.storage.local by the worker's refresh alarm, and only when the user has
Matching is exact-host OR any parent domain, so 'login.phish-demo.invalid' is caught by
'phish-demo.invalid'. A blocklist hit outranks everything, including the allowlist — that
asymmetry is on purpose: being wrong toward caution is survivable, the reverse is not.
`version` and `updatedAt` let the worker decide whether a fetched list supersedes this one.
